quotes.text:
It was also the behavior planned in the initial discussion:
"if you're not fixing versions in your roles file, then it's fine
to expect that the role will be reinstalled each time you run
ansible-galaxy install.", cf https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/12904
quotes.author: Michael Scherer
quotes.title: Fix --force for unversionned requirements (#23391)

quotes.text: * Improve force logic for galaxy version changes
quotes.author: Will Thames
quotes.title: Improve ansible-galaxy handling of role versions (#12904)

medium: The discussions highlight the necessity of this conditional to prevent unintended role reinstalls when versions are not explicitly defined.

card.what: This line checks if the `--force` flag is set; if it's not, the subsequent code block is executed.
card.why: The original intention was to allow `ansible-galaxy install` to reinstall roles even when versions weren't explicitly specified, aligning with the behavior discussed in the pull request [2]. Michael Scherer’s commit [1] highlights the fix for the `--force` flag specifically related to unversioned requirements, and Will Thames’s commit [3] further clarifies the logic around handling galaxy version changes.
card.next: Verify that the logic around `--force` still aligns with the desired behavior for reinstalling roles without version constraints.

answer: The outer conditional that handles force does not contain this branch, so force must be handled in both branches.
